guideline: Best-worst scaling for informativeness, coherence, and non-redundancy
Annotators were asked to select the best and worst summaries based on informativeness, coherence, and non-redundancy
Annotators were asked to judge summaries based on informativeness, coherence, non-redundancy (best-worst), content support level (full/partial/none), and aspect coverage (exclusive/partial/none).

We asked the annotators to select the best and worst summaries w.r.t. the following criteria: • Informativeness: How much useful information about the business does the summary provide? • Coherence: How coherent and easy to read is the summary? • Non-redanduncy: Is the summary successful at avoiding redundant and repeated opinions?

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. The paper focuses on abstractive opinion summarization using a pipeline approach combining ABSA extraction and Transformer generation. Human evaluation was comprehensive with multiple criteria. No LLMs were used for evaluation as this is a 2020 paper predating widespread LLM-as-judge practices.
